title_original: How Well Do You Know Your Artistic Icons?
excerpt_original: Take an interactive quiz to test your knowledge of the biggest names in art.

blocks.text: With a world in crisis and an art market spinning out of control, ace art-world consultants Chen & Lampert deliver a quiz full of hard choices for Art in America readers from far and wide.

The fall issue of Art in America honors artistic icons, and in recognition of their trailblazing singularity we’ve rejiggered the format of our usual quiz. Rather than answer questions about yourself, let’s find out what you know about the superstars, trendsetters, and groundbreakers whose audacity and cultural capital have reshaped the art world from a niche marketplace into a global duty-free mall. Correct answers are worth one point each, so tally up your score to find out how you fared.
1. He’s number one in our hearts for making number two in a metal can, sealing it shut, and calling it art:
a) Piero Manzoni b) Marcel Duchamp c) Andy Warhol
2. This artist invented his own color and threatened to sue people for using it:
a) Yves Klein b) Anish Kapoor c) Bob Ross
3. He locked himself inside a cage for a year as an artwork:
a) Joseph Beuys b) Tehching Hsieh c) Henry Darger
4. This person’s art involved voluntarily picking up NYC garbage and cleaning the streets for fun:
a) Pope.L b) Mierle Laderman Ukeles c) Yuji Agematsu
5. Interior Scroll is a performance classic in which this artist recites a rant retrieved from her vagina:
a) Carolee Schneemann b) Valie Export c) Florentina Holzinger
6. This storied gallerist served prison time for tax evasion:
a) Ileana Sonnabend b) Mary Boone c) Barbara Gladstone
7. Which prolific artist sired seven children with two wives and two other women?
a) Camille Pissarro b) Josh Kline c) Julian Schnabel
8. This funny man recently brought the yuks as a guest at Larry Gagosian’s 81st birthday party:
a) Louis C.K. b) Woody Allen c) Dave Chappelle
9. Which beloved artist used racist language to describe non-white people in their autobiography?
a) Edgar Degas b) Paul Gauguin c) Yayoi Kusama
10. Conned collector Charles C. Cahn Jr. sued Sotheby’s in 2025 for selling him a fake work by this irritable Italian imbiber:
a) Michelangelo Merisi da Caravaggio b) Amedeo Modigliani c) Maurizio Cattelan
SCORES
0-3: You didn’t do great, but you should feel good about finishing a magazine quiz in 2026. Buy yourself a smoothie as a reward.
4-7: You can make a dent in a cocktail-party conversation with an art academic or gallery attendant. They’ll walk away impressed by how you don’t blink when you talk.
8-10: Your art history PhD has finally paid off. Text your parents and update your LinkedIn with this iconic quiz score. Now, about those student loans…
